messages:
anya: flagging a weird bringup artifact for our new reranker (rank-slim-3B) after PTQ. ndcg@10 looks fine but MRR collapsed on the `forum-qa` cohort (titles+short queries). wondering if dataset curation or eval harness changed.
rob: interesting. what's the size of the cohort and the delta? any seed/retry variation?
anya: cohort=4.2k queries. fp16 mrr@10=0.578, int4-ptq mrr@10=0.512. ndcg@10 delta ~0.002. ran 3 sequential repeats, int4 shows consistent dip.
chris: consistent suggests systematic rather than noise. do the candidate pools match exactly between runs (dedupe, normalizers)? also check whether the eval harness applies the same gold pooling for forum-qa vs generic-holdout.
anya: candidate sources identical. noticed we recently switched on sparse-anchor filtering in candidate-generation for prod-only codepath; eval harness used the older candidate set. could be a catalog mismatch.
rob: ah that would change candidate distribution. two paths: 1) unify candidate-generation in eval to mirror prod sparse-anchor logic, 2) run paired A/B with same prod candidate set for fp16 vs int4 to isolate quant effect.
chris: also look at query/doc formatting: forum titles often have noise like [SOLVED], emojis, and code snippets that priming can amplify. quantized logits might reorder near ties. capture per-query top5 before/after and record margin histogram.
anya: started paired run A=fp16 prod-candidates B=int4-ptq prod-candidates. cmd: `./eval/pairwise.sh --cohort forum-qa --seed 13 --pairwise`
ml-ci: queued job 1855550001 (pairwise-forum-qa) on node-7 :gear:
ops-bot: reminder: attach tokenizer/version and preprocessing manifest to eval artifacts for reproducibility.
anya: results landed. paired metrics show top1-flip rate 3.1% and mean top1 score delta 0.014 for flipped queries. many flips concentrated where baseline top1-top2 margin < 0.02.
rob: that points to quant-induced perturbation amplified by tight margins. mitigation options: a) stable tie-breaker fallback to doc_uid, b) tiny rescale of logits before sorting for int4 to reduce flip sensitivity, c) keep prod sparse-anchor but add priming-safety for titles.
chris: prefer minimal-invasive: implement stable tie-breaker + add a per-cohort 'sensitivity test' in bringup that computes flip-rate and median margin. fail bringup if flip-rate > 2% for forum-qa. also log sample of 200 flipped queries' raw logits for investigation.
anya: will add stable-sort patch and bringup check. quick experiment: applied stable-docid tie-break and re-ran int4 -> top1-flip rate dropped to 0.8% and mrr recovered to 0.568. ndcg unchanged.
rob: nice. for long-term, we should standardize candidate-gen manifest in model artifacts and include a 'candidate-stability' checklist in onboarding docs. also decide whether to accept small flip-rate if unit-economics improvement is large.
chris: create a model-catalog note: "rank-slim-3B int4: expect small top1 flips on short-title cohorts; stable-tie policy enabled by default; recommend unified candidate manifest for eval vs prod."
ml-ci: opened ticket ML-2478 and attached artifacts (pairwise diffs, top5 logs, tokenizer-manifest).
anya: thanks all. i'll land the tie-break PR and rerun broader bringup afterwards. closing loop here.
